originality.rationale: Primary source explicitly proves four consecutive individual-weight flatness and optimality for p=1. Uniform sparse block-product rigidity for arbitrary block length together with all-length sharpness is a different hypothesis/conclusion pair. A powers-based deduction covers part of the rigidity, not the exhibited all-length sharpness construction. No stronger exact theorem was identified in actual source/index searches; residual risk acknowledged.
residual_risks: Known p=1 four-weight theorem and its application to powers substantially cover rigidity; only all-length sharpness/family is asserted as the extra contribution.
Nonindexed older general sparse-flatness or interpolation results might imply the construction.
Two ancillary related papers were not inspected completely; no claim of full-text negative coverage.

value.rationale: The number of consecutive equal products of p-edge windows is a natural finite rigidity cutoff, and identifying an optimal uniform cutoff for arbitrarily large window length is a structural property. The positivity-preserving all-p counterexample construction supplies a motivated and exact boundary beyond the known consecutive-weight p=1 result.
